messages:
nina: quick sanity check on the lightweight route grammar proposal?
chris: yes, can we try to make the precedence rules deterministic but simple for console users
leo: current problem: multiple routes tie when host and path specificity equal; console sorts by created_at which is confusing
adrian: agree. created_at is accidental. we should prefer structural rules not creation order
nina: proposal: score = (host_specificity*1000) + (path_specificity*10) + anchor_bonus
chris: define anchor_bonus? sounds fuzzy
nina: anchor_bonus = 5 if route has header anchors, 2 if has cookie anchors, 0 otherwise. keeps header-driven routes slightly preferred
leo: what about wildcards: longer literal prefix should beat an early wildcard even if same segment count
adrian: example: host=api.redwood.com vs host=*.redwood.com should always prefer exact host
chris: yeah exact host > subdomain wildcard > apex wildcard
nina: for path: /v1/users vs /v1/* -> /v1/users wins. segment literal count trumps capture
leo: edge: /v1/:id/profile vs /v1/:id/* -> profile wins because next segment is literal
adrian: tied routes with same anchor set and same scores -> deterministic tiebreak: fallback to lexicographic route id, not create_time
chris: lexicographic id is stable but leaks internal ids in ordering UX? fine though
nina: console should show reason: "matched by host specificity" etc. add match explain output to telemetry
leo: telemetry change: add fields: match_score, tiebreak_reason, matched_route_id
adrian: +1 on adding match_score. we can incrementally roll this
chris: rollout UX: add opt-in flag per workspace to use new scoring before global flip
nina: runtime cost concerns? scoring is tiny per route eval, but in extreme gateways (100k routes) we need precomputed scores and bloom filter short-circuit
leo: precompute score on route change, store in index. checks are O(1) for host/path buckets
adrian: header anchors: how do we treat negations? e.g., header X not set vs header X=foo
nina: negation should reduce anchor_bonus by 1 (we prefer positive anchors), but still count
chris: quota impact: if we re-order routes, can change per-route quotas observed in metrics. need to warn customers when flipping
leo: can we surface a dry-run telemetry mode that simulates new ordering and reports potential impacted routes and quota shifts? similar to rollout feature flags
adrian: yep, add a 'simulated_match' mode that runs in parallel and emits sample set to analytics bucket
nina: sample rate by default 0.1% to limit cost, adjustable by admins
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary to staging at 2026-04-05T03:00Z, if metrics look ok, promote to prod
chris: tests we need: unit for scoring, integration for explain output, load test for 100k routes
leo: also add e2e with header-negation combos
nina: action items: nina will write RFC draft with formula examples and sample telemetry schema; chris will prototype precompute index; adrian will spec console explain UX; leo will run quick sim on prod route snapshot
adrian: I'll own the dry-run telemetry endpoint
nina: thx, ping here when RFC draft is up
chris: thanks all :thumbsup:
